title: Permission-checked message search: Session Core index with per-hit re-authorization and ZDR exclusion, in-room scoped search on Ctrl/Cmd+F and open-in-context
summary: Add a keyword index over Space thread messages in Session Core and a SearchSpaceMessages call plus gateway route; the index only proposes candidates, every hit is re-authorized against the Control room-read decision and audience revision, and ZDR or privacy-restricted turns are never indexed. In the room, Ctrl/Cmd+F opens a search with a removable scope chip (room, thread, person, global), and hits open in context through thread and entry deep links plus cursor paging of the thread list.
whyItMatters: There is no message, thread or room search at all; four references treat permission-aware search as table stakes, and a room people work in for months is unusable without it. The index must not ship before Session Core enforces ZDR.

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-04-01] 4 of 5 sources; table-stakes [R-t1-04-02] 4 of 5 sources; table-stakes
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-04-01] Postgres STORED generated tsvector column (simple config) on the message table with a GIN index; sensitive kinds produce a NULL tsvector so they never match; every query requires a tenant/community id. The engine reads candidates in pages of about 100 ordered by ts_rank, re-fetches each through a scoped fetcher and applies the access predicate per hit, so a page can be shorter than the limit. A prefix mode (to_tsquery with :*) serves typeahead. Teams adds suggestions, search-history and click-feedback endpoints and a query-alteration (spelling) field, which inform the API shape only. [R-t1-04-02] Teams offers channel, chat, community, thread, post and a people-centred scope (files, messages, images with a person), each discoverable from autosuggest with a shortcut hint. Slack routes the native Find command to in-app search; buzz shows a removable scope chip. Esc or backspace on the chip widens to global search; people-centred mode filters by author or participant id.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: [R-t1-04-01] No Space, thread or message search route or index exists. Gateway search.rs routes are web, image, video, suggest and answer (Quarry-backed) only (SRC, re-read in this step), and conversation search exists only for the support inbox. The pieces a hit needs to open in context are also missing (see this item (R-t1-04-02)). [R-t1-04-02] Only a client-side filter over room names and the selected room's thread titles and previews exists. It never searches message bodies, other rooms, one thread or a person, and Ctrl+F is not routed to it. Thread deep links (?thread_id=) are generated in activity-grammar.ts but no code under src/features/spaces reads a search param (grep in this step), and the thread list has no paging, so a hit could not be opened in context.

approachOriginal: [R-t1-04-01] Session Core (Model Plane): add a generated tsvector plus GIN index over message text on origin=space threads, NULL for turns stamped ZDR or privacy-restricted; add gRPC SearchSpaceMessages(space_id, query, filters{authors, since, until, is, has}, cursor) returning {thread_id, message_seq, snippet with highlights, author, ts}. Candidates are paged by rank and filtered with the same audience-revision predicate the room transcript read already uses (spaces.rs space_thread_transcript, which Session Core enforces by dropping rows newer than the decision revision). Gateway adds GET /api/v1/spaces/{ref}/search that obtains the Control read decision exactly as the transcript route does and forwards it; client-supplied scope is never trusted. Start keyword-only; evaluate stemming for Norwegian/English mixes (simple config has none). [R-t1-04-02] Frontend Plane: scope chip plus Ctrl/Cmd+F handler in SpacePage calling the this item (R-t1-04-01) gateway route with space_id (and thread_id or author filters). Keep the sidebar filter for instant title matching and fall through to server results. Make SpacePage consume ?thread_id=&seq= (scroll to and highlight the message) and add cursor paging with jump-to-message to the thread read path. Offer a fallback to the browser find bar when in-app search is unavailable.
dependencies: Session Core must act on the ZDR claim (baseline: decoded but ignored today); do not ship the index before this
Reuse of the Control room-read decision and audience-revision predicate (spaces.rs:2616-2736)
Non-owner reply fix if search should also cover replies by other members
Thread list cursor paging and deep-link consumption in SpacePage
planeOwner: Model Plane (Session Core index and search) with Frontend Plane (gateway route, search UI) and Control Plane (read decision)
risks: [R-t1-04-01] Indexing content that ZDR forbids persisting; search treated as an access boundary instead of a candidate source (always post-filter); revocation lag because membership_changed is plain, lossy NATS; no stemming with the simple config. [R-t1-04-02] Overriding browser Ctrl+F annoys users if in-app search is weaker; a deep link to a message the viewer can no longer read must fail closed.

verevon.exactGap: There is no Space message, thread or room search: the gateway search router serves only web, similar, suggest, images, videos, suggestions and answer; Ctrl/Cmd+K opens GlobalSearchDialog over Data v2 knowledge plus client-side chat history; and the sidebar filter matches only room names and the selected room's thread titles and previews. Session Core has no tsvector or GIN index on messages (Data v2 retrieval-engine-rs has one, but for documents) and no SearchSpaceMessages RPC, the Space thread list takes only a limit with no cursor, and ?thread_id= deep links are never consumed, so a hit could not open in context. The ZDR blocker the item names is already cleared in code, because Session Core refuses durable writes from ZDR callers and so never stores ZDR content to index.
reuse: Session Core audience-revision read predicate (grpc.rs:5455-5461) for per-hit filtering.
The Space-scoped shared read decision used by space_thread_transcript (spaces.rs:2606-2700), which is requested per Space rather than per thread and so can authorize a room-wide query.
idx_messages_author_subject (migration 0035) for a 'from person' filter.
CoreSidebarSpacesPanel title filter for instant client-side matching with server results as fallthrough.
Data v2 sparse.rs websearch_to_tsquery plus ts_rank_cd as a reference for the query shape only.
verevon.constraints: Message text is owned by Session Core: do not copy transcripts into Data v2 or Convex for search, because that creates a second durable store of Space content (and a ZDR problem). The index only proposes candidates; every hit is re-filtered by the audience-revision predicate and a fresh Control read decision, and revoked members stay denied (revocations arrive over plain NATS events, so check on every query). Postgres 'simple' text config has no Norwegian stemming, so start keyword-only. A deep link to a message the viewer can no longer read must fail closed.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Remove the ZDR prerequisite (already enforced by the Session Core write refusal) and keep the first slice keyword-only. Use one Space-scoped read decision per query, as space_thread_transcript does, instead of per-thread decisions. Ship the thread-list cursor and the ?thread_id=&seq= deep link in the same slice as the search UI, otherwise hits cannot open in context. Author filters are cheap because messages already store author_subject_id.
verevon.verdictReason: Verified absent in Session Core, gateway and UI; the item is accurate and its ZDR dependency is already met, so only the approach notes change.

title: Let room agents call Space actions themselves (agent self-API with run-bound grants)
summary: Admit a vetted subset of the typed spaces.* actions, plus new agent-oriented ones (create thread, post card, schedule follow-up, pin or rename a thread, pause self), to the model-executable set so a room agent can do what a human member can without a bespoke tool per action. Model Plane consumes the Frontend action registry as a staged-disclosure tool catalogue, Control Plane mints run-bound capability grants, and the gateway dispatcher re-checks the delegating human's ACL on every call; risky actions route to the existing in-room approval card.
whyItMatters: This is the core of 'agents that work like a human': today a room agent can only talk, because none of the 14 registered spaces.* actions is model-eligible. qm and buzz show the payoff (agents organise threads, schedule their own follow-ups, invite or pin) and Verevon already has the right catalogue shape (typed registry with risk level and owner plane per action), so the cost is low relative to the value.

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 5 sources; differentiator (absent from the human-chat incumbents)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: qm serves a discoverable /v1/apis catalogue: API families with guidance text and eligibility predicates (role, feature flag). The runtime signs a capability token per durable run (claims: org, principal, session, run attempt, expiry; 48 h default) sent as x-agent-capability, and every handler re-verifies the principal's authority per call, so admin work reuses the same handlers. Buzz mirrors every action as a JSON-in/JSON-out CLI subcommand over signed events, the most ergonomic shape for shell-driven agents.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: MODEL_EXECUTABLE_ACTION_IDS holds 8 entries (tickets.create, inbox.*, chat.*, org.*) and none of the 14 spaces.* actions. The admission bar is strict by design: owner-issued durable receipt, idempotent fencing and forged-call denial proven on both sides (SRC, model-eligibility.ts header). Model Gateway's inline read lane deliberately has no write actions because it has no approval gate. The Space action catalogue endpoint is human-only with no UI consumer, and there is no run-bound grant for agent-originated Space actions. Several existing actions (add/remove member, revoke agent, request deletion) must stay human-only; the plan (S3.6) says agents may request use but never change future authority. The most agent-useful actions (create thread, schedule follow-up) are not registry actions yet (INF).

approachOriginal: Model Plane (capability-core / execution-core): list eligible registry actions to the agent with staged disclosure (as mcp_catalog does) and dispatch them through the governed agentic path, not the read-only inline loop. Control Plane: add a run-bound grant decision (principal, Space, run id, action allowlist, expiry) following the existing model.cron.create / model.cron.fire decision pattern. Frontend gateway dispatcher: accept the grant, re-derive the delegating human's membership from Control and audit exactly like a UI call. Admit actions one at a time under the model-eligibility.ts bar, starting with low-risk idempotent ones (update_thread_presentation, set_agent_state for itself, new create_thread and schedule actions); keep membership, role, deletion and credential-grant changes human-only and send medium/high-risk calls to the approval card via approval continuation. Optional later: a thin JSON CLI for sandboxed agent computers (buzz style) over the same dispatcher.
dependencies: Per-action admission under the model-eligibility.ts bar (owner receipt, idempotency, forged-call denial)
New agent-oriented spaces.* actions in the registry
planeOwner: Model Plane (catalogue and dispatch); Control Plane mints grants; Frontend Plane owns the action registry
risks: Prompt injection driving membership, role or visibility changes; destructive actions must stay approval-gated and audited; Space access must never widen the owner-plane ACL, so the grant must intersect with the delegating human's authority on every call.

verevon.exactGap: A governed agent-to-owner action pipeline is built end to end for exactly one action, tickets.create: Control model-action-view and run-action-decision plus owner-effect reservation (run_action_decision.go:340-347, model_action_view.go:18-26), Capability Core advertising (capability-core model_action_view.go:21-32), the execution-core adapter (ticket_tools.rs) and approval continuation, all hard-coded to that one action and schema hash. MODEL_EXECUTABLE_ACTION_IDS has 8 entries and none of the 14 spaces.* registry actions (model-eligibility.ts:126-135, action-registry.ts:1991-2134); the Space actions catalogue is human-only (spaces.rs:4880-4925). Room agents are also born tool-less and confirmation-only, which strips tools and agentic mode on mention turns (spaceAgents.ts:540-565, spaces.rs:4519-4535).
reuse: Control RunActionDecision (run id, thread, Space ref, subject, schema hash, payload digest, idempotency key, audience revision, expiry) and OwnerEffectReservationCommitment: the existing per-call, run-bound authority, to be generalized instead of inventing a new grant type
tickets.create pipeline (ticket_tools.rs, capability-core model_action_view.go, execution-core approval continuation and approval_delivery_worker) as the template for each admitted action
Owner-issued agent-action-grants routes per conversation (spaces.rs:665-675) as the human-granted standing allowance
SpaceApprovalPanel and orchestration approvals as the in-room approval card
Model-Plane-owned operations (thread presentation lives in model-gateway/session-core) as same-plane tools that need no cross-plane grant
verevon.constraints: Model proposes, owner executes: each admitted action needs an owner-side endpoint that verifies a Control run-action decision and rechecks its own ACL (the run's thread authorization is explicitly not authority for a target resource, run_action_decision.go:19-22). Capability Core deliberately uses a server-owned schema, not a Frontend registry copy (capability-core model_action_view.go:29-32), so the Model Plane must not consume the Frontend action registry. Membership, role, deletion and credential-grant changes stay human-only (plan S3.6: agents may request use, never change future authority). Room agents are tool-less and confirmation-only by default and a run belongs to the member who started it, so approvals are decided by the run owner. ZDR forbids durable owner actions (personal_thread_decision.go:292-294).
verevon.approachAdjustment: Do not mint a new 'run-bound capability grant'; extend the existing run-action decision: add one runActionTarget entry per action (today only tickets.create is approved), generalize model-action-view and Capability Core from one fixed action to a server-owned list, and add an owner endpoint per owning plane. Do not have the Model Plane consume the Frontend registry: the registry feeds the browser (agent-tools.ts), while the Model Plane holds its own pinned schemas. Phase it: first Model-Plane-owned tools bound to the run's own thread (rename or pin the thread, post a card), which need no cross-plane decision; then Application-owned ones (pause self) and orchestrator-owned ones (schedule follow-up) through the run-action path. Also make binding policy editable, otherwise no room agent can use tools at all.
verevon.effortNote: Raised from M. Each action needs an owner endpoint, a Control decision target, a pinned schema and an execution-core adapter, and the single-action machinery must first be generalized.
verevon.verdictReason: The capability is genuinely missing for Spaces, but a run-bound decision mechanism already exists for one action and the item's grant and registry-consumption design conflicts with it; rewrite as generalizing that pipeline in phases.

title: Room-scoped agent browser: space_ref on browser runs, a live preview card that expands to an interactive view, hand-off and take-over with a control indicator
summary: Add a space_ref to the browser run start request and authorize it with a Control decision for the room audience, show browser steps and evidence as room cards, and let the room watch the session as a glanceable preview card that expands to an interactive modal (screen switcher, 'control: agent | you' badge, idle pause) in the AuxPane. Add a hand-off request (id plus instruction), Take control and I'm done, and bot-wall detection that hands off instead of retrying. Quarry still executes every action; the Model only proposes.
whyItMatters: The brief asks for agents that work like a person with their own browser. Browser runs exist and the gateway already serves live frames with human takeover, but nothing is Space-scoped, so the room cannot see, attribute or govern the agent's browsing.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: qm (browser model grant); grokbot (hosted browser, live takeover, bot-wall detection); Grok Bot (preview card to interactive modal, multi-screen, control owner badge)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-07-06] Agent browser 2 of 5 (differentiator); live view and take-over 1 of 5 (unique); teach by demonstration 1 of 5 (unique) [R-t1-12-08] 1 of 5 (Grok Bot); unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-07-06] QM core mints a capability token {browserModel, browserAccount, aud browser-model}; the browser runner calls an OpenAI-style completions endpoint at core, so it never holds a provider key; 409 if the person's account or model changed; sign-in profiles are held as credentials and shown only in DMs. Grok Bot classifies bot-check walls from URL/title and hands off instead of retrying; LiveState carries box_handoff_request_id plus an instruction; EndHandoff trigger BUTTON|VIEWER_CLOSED|DISMISSED; the live view is an embedded noVNC page with token-to-header injection, phase reporting and pause when hidden. Grok Bot teach mode: recording START|SAVE|DISCARD, the saved recording is sent as a message with initiator TEACH_RECORDING so a skill is authored in chat. [R-t1-12-08] Computer view modes {preview, interactive}: preview is a periodic frame or low-rate VNC stream in a card; the modal is interactive VNC with a screen switcher and a control-owner badge (agent or you); an idle pause with wake and retry; a REC overlay while recording.

title: Agent computer confinement: real network enforcement and resource caps, audience-bound egress, one SSRF-safe connector
summary: Finish the agent-computer boundary. First, make egress real: run processes whose policy allows domains in a network namespace whose only route is the egress proxy (today the executor only checks that a proxy variable is set), add cgroup or rlimit caps, apply the seccomp or Landlock layers that the code comments name, and require a sandbox-manager lease for every Space agent. Second, compute an effective egress allowlist per room from the audience snapshot (intersection of members' lists, union of denies), bind it into the signed decision and enforce it in Quarry and the sandbox proxy with audited allow and deny. Third, share one SSRF-safe connector for unfurls, webhooks and agent fetches.
whyItMatters: Grok-Bot-style agent computers are part of the Space vision, and confinement is the real security boundary under every softer control. A room-aware egress rule fits 'Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL': an agent acting for a room must not reach a destination any member's org forbids.

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Sandbox confinement: 1 of 5 (grokbot); egress policy: 2 of 5 (grokbot, qm); SSRF-safe fetch: 2 of 5 (buzz, grokbot). Differentiator.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A launcher takes a declarative policy {type: readonly or workspace read-write, writable roots, network: none or proxy}; on Linux it uses bubblewrap, Landlock and seccomp plus a cgroup v2 attach per process with OOM reset, and file APIs resolve real paths and refuse anything outside the root. For rooms, audienceEgressFloor intersects every member's allowlists and unions denies, binds the result to the turn and logs decisions at the proxy. SSRF: resolve the host, require a global unicast address (reject private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT, mapped and NAT64 forms), connect to the pinned IP with the original SNI, re-validate on redirects.

title: Room administration basics: change and choose member roles with an owner guard, rename, topic, archive and restore, and keep the organization room roster in sync
summary: Add a per-member role change and a role choice on add (viewer, editor, manager, owner) instead of the fixed editor grant, with Buzz-style pure guard functions (canGrant, canChangeRole, canLeave, last-owner rule) and table tests. Let managers rename a room and edit its topic, archive and unarchive it (read-only archive), and let owners or org admins delete it with a restore window once shared-room deletion lands on the saga (see the retention item). Run the existing syncAllOrganizationRooms on a schedule and on org membership changes so new members appear in the organization room and removed members leave it.
whyItMatters: Control already has viewer/editor/manager/owner roles and lifecycle states, but no route or UI changes a role, shared rooms cannot be renamed or archived, and the organization room's roster is never re-synced after provisioning. title: Client resilience: root and per-region error boundaries, lazy-chunk recovery, a boot watchdog, and a build id with stale-tab reload and contract guard
summary: Wrap the app in a root error boundary plus per-region boundaries (navbar, Space cockpit, side panels, run console) that show a classified failure card (render error, stale-deploy chunk failure, session expired, gateway unreachable) with Reload and Retry; reload once on a chunk-preload failure with a loop guard; add a boot watchdog. Expose a build id (Vite define plus a no-store version.json) and a minimum-client/contract version from the gateway, show a non-blocking 'new version, reload' banner, and force reload only on a contract mismatch after drafts are saved.
whyItMatters: The code itself states there is no Suspense or ErrorBoundary, so one render error blanks a Space that people keep open all day, and a tab open across a deploy keeps an old bundle whose lazy chunks can 404. Both are cheap to fix and immediately visible to users.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: teams (diagnosis-specific error curtain with Restart / Repair / Open on web); grokbot (per-feature minimum client versions with a machine-readable update-required hint)
others: slack (fatal-exception and unresponsive-window dialogs with telemetry flush)
grokbot (single restore lifecycle with a 30 s stuck detector that reports the stage reached)
teams (staged nag-then-block staleness policy, DOC only)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-11-02] 3 of 5 sources (slack, teams, grokbot) = common; every native reference invests heavily here. [R-t1-11-04] 2 of 5 sources (grokbot, teams) = differentiator.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-11-02] Root boundary catches render and chunk-load failures and shows a curtain with a classified cause and actions; watchdog timers on boot stages emit "stuck at stage X" telemetry; hang detection offers wait or reload; safe-mode switches. [R-t1-11-04] Remote config {min_version, feature_min_versions, max_age_days}; API responses carry a CLIENT_UPDATE_REQUIRED hint when a stale client calls a gated feature; the UI turns the hint into a banner or forced reload.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: [R-t1-11-02] The createResource shim comment states the app has zero Suspense/ErrorBoundary usage, and src/index.tsx renders <App/> directly. A grep over src (excluding demo) for ErrorBoundary, Errored, Loading, unhandledrejection and vite:preloadError finds only that comment. About 30 routes are lazy() imports, and nginx answers a missing hashed .js file with 404 (try_files $uri =404), so a stale chunk after deploy has no recovery path. Only per-feature typed error states exist (for example budget_exceeded in the Space composer). [R-t1-11-04] No build id or version is exposed to the client (comparator grep for buildId, __APP_VERSION__, version.json found nothing; my grep of import.meta.env use shows only demo, captcha and gateway-url toggles). A tab open across a deploy keeps the old bundle, lazy chunks can 404, and there is no "reload" prompt. The SSE reader already supports Last-Event-ID resume, which is a natural hook for the version check.

approachOriginal: [R-t1-11-02] Frontend Plane: use the boundary primitive of the Solid version in use (the shim comment names Errored/Loading for Solid 2) at the root and around each shell region; failure card component with i18n copy keyed by error code (reuse shared/i18n/errors.ts) and a request id; window listener for the Vite preload-error event that reloads once (sessionStorage guard) and otherwise shows the card; boot-stage recorder posting to the existing gateway observability route (apps/gateway/src/domains/monitoring.rs). Report action uses the ids-only flow in F-t1-079 (R-t1-11-08). [R-t1-11-04] Frontend Plane: Vite build id injected at build, emitted as /version.json (Cache-Control: no-store; add an explicit nginx location, because json files currently fall through to the SPA fallback at nginx.conf:131-133 with no cache header, and give index.html no-cache too); gateway adds an X-Verevon-Client-Min header (or /api/v1/client-config) next to the existing envelope; SPA store compares on visibilitychange and SSE reconnect, shows the banner, and hard-reloads on a contract-version mismatch after the draft store flushes. An optional "What is new" entry can render once per build id from the deploy pipeline (low value, one-day follow-on).
dependencies: Persistent composer drafts (F-t1-032 (R-t1-01-08)) before any forced reload
risks: [R-t1-11-02] Boundaries that swallow errors silently; always report with a request id. Auto-reload must not lose an unsent composer draft (see F-t1-032 (R-t1-01-08)). [R-t1-11-04] Forced reloads during typing lose drafts; version skew between the gateway and Space event schemas must be a deliberate contract version, not the build hash.

verevon.exactGap: The production app has no ErrorBoundary/Errored, Loading/Suspense, vite:preloadError, unhandledrejection or boot-watchdog code: index.tsx renders App directly, about 30 routes are lazy() imports (App.tsx:1-37), and the only trace is the shim comment saying the app has zero Suspense/ErrorBoundary usage (create-resource-compat.ts:3-9). nginx answers a missing hashed asset with 404 (nginx.conf:103-114) and serves index.html and any version.json with no cache header (nginx.conf:132-133), vite.config.ts defines no build id, and no client-version or contract header exists at the gateway (main.rs:213-221 only reports the server revision at /version). Only per-feature typed error states exist (for example SpaceRoomComposer onError, :458-467, and the code-keyed copy in shared/i18n/errors.ts).
reuse: Solid 2 rc.0 exports Errored, Loading and createErrorBoundary (solid.js:1117), the primitives the shim comment says the app lacks
shared/i18n/errors.ts code-to-copy seam and ApiError/extractError (sse.ts, http.ts) for classified failure cards
SSE reader Last-Event-ID resume (sse.ts:25-60) as the reconnect hook for a version check
Gateway /version (main.rs:213-221) already reports the deployed revision and build date; gateway Prometheus metrics (observability.rs) for server-side counters
verevon.constraints: Frontend Plane only, but a forced reload must not drop an unsent composer draft, so it depends on the draft store. Telemetry must not carry message content or user data and must respect ZDR (ids only). The browser reaches the gateway only through nginx /api/ and /health (nginx.conf proxy locations), so a gateway /version at the root is not reachable by the SPA without a new /api route.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Fix one pointer: apps/gateway/src/domains/monitoring.rs is Quarry change-monitoring (URL check, latest, history), not an observability sink, and observability.rs only exposes server Prometheus metrics. There is no client error or boot-stage endpoint and no global request-id in the envelope, so add a small ids-only client-diagnostics route under /api/v1 (or drop the boot-stage recorder from this item) and add request-id middleware if the failure card must show one. Everything else in the approach (root and region boundaries with Errored, one-time reload on chunk-preload failure with a sessionStorage guard, version.json with no-store plus an explicit nginx location and index.html no-cache, gateway min-client header or client-config, non-blocking banner, forced reload only on contract mismatch) is sound.
verevon.effortNote: Raised from S. Boundaries plus chunk recovery plus a build-id banner is S; the gateway contract-version header, a client-diagnostics route and draft-safe forced reload make the full item M.
verevon.verdictReason: Nothing of this exists in production code, so the recommendation stands, but it points at the wrong gateway route for observability and understates effort.
